rationale: This mixed-methods case study of Mebane, North Carolina combines GIS spatial analysis of 2000 Census demographic data and geocoded sewer/zoning records with participant observation and content analysis of town council deliberations. Its central legal-institutional mechanism is municipal underbounding—specifically the strategic drawing of municipal corporate limits, selective annexation, and Extra-Territorial Jurisdiction (ETJ) boundary governance (`institutional_structure_coordination`), reinforced by selective local official discretion in land-use/watershed overlays (`discretion_accommodation`)—used to exclude historic African American neighborhoods from the city limits and thereby deny them municipal sewer line extensions (`primary_connection`).
